citations.B1: Read-then-write race: two threads can both read `count = 99`
citations.B2: two threads can both read `count = 99` and both write 100, so the limit is exceeded
citations.B4: No time window: counts only ever grow, so a user is permanently banned after 100 lifetime requests
citations.B5: Unbounded memory growth: `counts` never evicts, so one entry per user forever is a memory leak
citations.B6: each process/gunicorn worker has its own `counts`, so the real limit is `limit × workers`
citations.B7: No handling of `user_id=None` or unauthenticated callers
